text:
name: move_savings
does: Moves money between your own accounts, for example from savings to the account you keep for tax.
inputs: the account to take money from, the account to put it in, and how much; it works for a gold card account too, and you can pack a few moves into one request
people say:
- put two hundred into my tax account
- shift some money from savings to checking
- I need fifty more in my current account
- send half of my savings over to the holiday account
- take thirty from checking and park it in savings

Many phones can read text aloud. This helps people who cannot see small letters well, or who have busy hands. Imagine a cook standing at the sink, ready to wash a pot, who wants to hear a message. The cook can ask the phone to read it out. If the voice is too fast, people say "slow down" or "speak slower". If the words are too small, they say "make the text bigger". If the phone says a word the wrong way, people can ask it to spell the word, so they get the correct reading. Some people even have a message about their salary read to them on the bus. Everyone can also pick a voice they like and make it louder or softer.

A young person wants to hear more headlines, perhaps about milk prices or a player who will heal soon.
more news please
give me a few more headlines
is there more?
read me double the headlines this time
I'd like to hear more stories than just the top three
can you keep going with the news
tell me a couple more sports results
could you please read a few more headlines, I haven't heard enough yet

Zeynep woke up late and blinked at the ceiling. The kitchen was quiet. Zeynep reached for the phone and said, "Hey, what is on my list for this Saturday afternoon?" The phone read out three tasks: buy a can of soup, weigh the parcel for Auntie, and fix the gate on the north side of the garden. Zeynep yawned. "Check off the parcel. I did that last night," Zeynep said. The phone marked it as done and said two tasks were left. "Move the gate to the top, because rain is coming," Zeynep added. The phone put the gate first and read the list again, so Zeynep could hear the new order. Then Zeynep smiled and went to make tea.

name: low_stock_check
does: Looks at your shopping list and your fridge notes and tells you what is running out, so you never feel stuck without it and can buy extra of the things you use most.
inputs: the food or item to check, and how much you use each day, like a spoon of coffee or a cup of milk
people say:
- are we out of eggs?
- do I need to buy more rice
- what's running low in the kitchen
- check if there's any butter left
- remind me what we're nearly out of
- how much milk do we have left

Someone wants to know if it will be a pretty day outside, so they can serve lunch in the garden or keep the coat in the cupboard.
weather?
how's it looking outside
is it going to rain today
what's it like out there right now
do I need a coat today
will it be above fifteen degrees by lunchtime
I'm planning lunch in the garden, will it be nice out
could you tell me what the weather will do this afternoon
would you mind checking whether it is likely to rain later today, please

People often want to know how many days are left until a big day, like a birthday or a trip. A phone can do the counting for you. You say the date, and it says a number. Grandma might want to hear how many days are left until the family visit, so a child asks, "How many days until Grandma's birthday?" People change the question by saying "no, the twentieth" or "I meant next month". They can also ask for weeks instead of days, with words like "how many weeks" or "how many sleeps". A countdown can stay on the screen, so you can look at it every morning and see the number get smaller.

A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see a baby in another room. It is for staying close while the baby naps. Many parents set a number of hours between feedings and ask the speaker to remind them. They say things like "remind me to feed the baby in three hours" or "move the nap alarm later". Sometimes the monitor makes a false alarm, because a cat walked by or a blanket moved. Then people say "turn the sensitivity down" or "stop the alerts for an hour". A parent can also ask to look at the camera by saying "show me the baby's room", and the screen lights up with the picture.

Scaling a recipe means making more or less food from the same steps. A cake for four people can become a cake for eight if you use double the flour, sugar and eggs. People ask for this by saying "make this for six" or "cut the recipe in half". Cups and spoons matter too, so a helper can turn cups into spoons, or tell you how many servings you will get. Some cooks take a breath and smile when the helper says there will be enough for everyone. If you like your food mild, you can ask for less pepper by saying "go easy on the spice".

Etienne was texting on the bus when a worry came. Grandpa lived alone, and his phone battery was always flat by noon. Etienne typed to the assistant: "grandpa never answers after lunch and I can't tell if he took his pills". The assistant understood that Etienne wanted a check-in. It set up a call to Grandpa for four o'clock and looked at the pill reminder to see if today's dose was marked. It was not. So the assistant sent a gentle message to the tablet that Grandpa had on loan from the school club, telling him to take his pills. Then Etienne typed, "remove the old reminder for Tuesday, he has a doctor visit". The assistant removed it and said the call was still set.

Person: I lost my cap at the park.
Assistant: Oh no. Which park was it?
Person: The one by the school. It's important, I need it for the school trip in ten days.
Assistant: Okay. Do you want me to post a message in the neighbourhood group?
Person: Yes please. Say it is blue.
Assistant: I wrote: blue cap lost near the school park. The message will stretch across the whole street group, so many neighbours will see it. Should I put a phone number on it?
Person: Put my mum's number.
Assistant: I can't use a number I don't have, and I can't share a child's number without a grown-up saying yes. Can you ask your mum to tell me it?

Amani was hungry and wanted to be the first customer at the bakery when it opened at eight. Before leaving, Amani typed on the phone: "is it gonna rian this morning". The phone answered that there would be no rain until ten, so the walk was safe. Amani smiled. Then Amani noticed that the morning reminder had been turned off by mistake and said, "undo that". The phone brought the reminder back and said it was on again for tomorrow at seven. Amani put the phone in a pocket, picked up the shopping bag, and walked out into the dry morning.

Person: How do I say "clean the filter of the air purifier" in German?
Assistant: Sure. Is it for a note, or do you want to learn to say it out loud?
Person: A note. My babysitter comes in ten days and she only reads German.
Assistant: Bitte reinigen Sie den Filter des Luftreinigers. The word Luftreiniger is a bit rare, though. Many people just say Luftfilter. Which one do you want?
Person: Use the common one, please. And can you text it to her?
Assistant: I can't send it, because I don't have her number. Can you give it to me, or do you want to copy the note yourself?
Person: I'll copy it myself. Thank you.

Home electricity use is how much power your house uses each day. People watch it to save money and avoid waste. Many use a smart plug or a small meter to see the numbers. A child may play a video game for hours, and the meter shows that the power goes up. People say "how much power did we use today?", "turn off the heater at night" or "keep the lights at half brightness". Solar panels on a roof, set at a good height to catch the sun, make power from daylight. Many families ask "how much did the panels make today?" and then choose when to run the washing machine.

name: leave_by_alarm
does: Sets an alarm for the time you must leave, working back from when you need to arrive and how long the drive takes.
inputs: the time you must arrive, how long the trip takes, and whether it is a busy time of day; it can also switch on a plug for the coffee machine
people say:
- wake me early enough to get to work by nine
- remind me to go ten minutes before the bus
- tell me when to set off for dinner at seven
- make sure I leave in time for school drop-off
- I have to be at the station by noon, when should I get up?

Baraka was in the garden when the shed door stuck. The key was in the lock but would not turn. Baraka wiped muddy hands and typed on the phone: "find somone to fix my shed lock tomorrow". The phone found two repair people near town and asked which one Baraka liked. Baraka chose the one with better reviews. Then Baraka said the repair person should also paint the door, because the wood was wet and that was important. The phone booked a visit for nine the next morning and added a note about the paint. It said a message would come an hour before the visit.

Andre came home after a bad night shift at the hospital. All Andre wanted was warm bread. The dough was in a bowl on the counter, and it had to climb to twice its size before baking. Andre told the kitchen speaker, "Remind me to heat the oven in an hour, and what was the weight of the flour in this recipe?" The speaker set a reminder for one hour from then. After that it said the recipe used five hundred grams of flour. Andre nodded, covered the bowl with a towel, and lay down on the sofa. An hour later the speaker called out softly that it was time to turn on the oven.

A neighbourhood group chat is a place where people on one street share news. It is for lost pets, noise, and local events like a street party. People change how often they hear from it by saying "mute the group for a day" or "only tell me about big news". If a dog is lost, a neighbour can tag the post with the words "lost pet", so others find it fast. A perfect post says what happened, where, and when. If a bike goes missing, people also write its colour and brand, so someone who sees it can say so. Later they can say "close the post" when the problem is solved.

Kevin was a cook, and flour was all over the cook's hands. Kevin could not touch the screen, so Kevin said to the phone, "Read my new messages out loud, but don't read the long ones from the work group." The phone read two short messages. One was from a friend: bring a hoodie to the picnic, and pack some neat snacks. Kevin laughed. Then Kevin squinted at the screen and said, "Make the text bigger. I don't want the small letters." The phone made the letters bigger, and now Kevin could read them from across the kitchen.

Radio is sound sent through the air to a small box in your home, your car or your phone. It is for news, music and talk. You pick a station by its name or its number. People say "put on the news", "switch to the music station" or "turn it down". A smart speaker can play the radio too, so a family can listen while they bathe the baby or cook dinner. The last thing many people do before leaving is hear the weather report. Some people even ask the radio to play a song for a friend's birthday, like a small present.

name: parcel_tracker
does: Shows where an online order is now and when it will arrive, even if it was a cheap order from a small shop.
inputs: the order number, the shop, or what you ordered, like an apron
people say:
- where's my package?
- when will my apron get here
- has the parcel left the warehouse yet
- is my order late
- check what I bought last week
- did the delivery person come today

Someone in the neighborhood wants a soft reminder to take their pills every day, so they don't have to push themselves to remember.
pill reminder please
remind me about my tablets each morning
don't let me forget my medicine
every day at eight, tell me to take my heart pill
ping me when it's pill time
I always forget my pills, could you nudge me every day after breakfast
the pharmacy gave me a bottle with two hundred tablets, so please remind me every morning to take one
would you be so kind as to remind me of my medicine at lunchtime each day

Agnieszka drove a delivery van and was scared of missing the team call about the company picnic. At a red light, Agnieszka said, "Please set up a meeting with the team before lunch on Sunday, to plan the picnic." The assistant found a free time, sent the invitations, and said the meeting was set for eleven on Sunday. Then Agnieszka remembered that the van needed a repair. "Put the van repair on the agenda," Agnieszka said. The assistant made it the second item and read the agenda back. By the time the light turned green, everything was done, and Agnieszka could keep both eyes on the road.

Sakura was not good with technology and did not like asking for help. But the doctor had said to walk more, so Sakura picked up the phone and said slowly, "Excuse me, could you please tell me how many steps I have walked today, because my doctor wants me to get some fresh air and I would like to know if I did enough?" The phone said four thousand two hundred steps. Then Sakura asked how to spell the word "pedometer", which a man had said on the tv. The phone spelled it one letter at a time. Sakura wrote it down on a small card and smiled.

Person: The shirt on the floor display says forty euros, and I never know what that means for me.
Assistant: I can help. Which money do you use at home?
Person: Pounds. I am not good with these things.
Assistant: No problem. Forty euros is about thirty-four pounds today. Should I show you a short list for other prices too?
Person: Yes please. The pound seems strong this month.
Assistant: It has been a little stronger than last month. Do you want ten, twenty and fifty euros?
Person: Yes, that would be good.
Assistant: Ten euros is about eight and a half pounds, twenty is about seventeen, and fifty is about forty-three.

Giorgio stood at the bus stop in the rain. Mum was at work, so Giorgio held the phone with two cold hands. "Next bus?" Giorgio asked. The phone said the number nine bus would come in six minutes. The roof of the shelter had a leak, and drops fell on Giorgio's shoe, so Giorgio moved to the dry side. "Which stop is mine?" Giorgio asked. The phone said the school stop was the fourth one. When the bus came, the rain stopped and the sky turned clear. Giorgio got on and found a seat by the window.

Ruta was texting on the sofa. The room felt dry, so Ruta typed to the phone: "Can you order a humidifier for me? The gold one from the shop I looked at yesterday." Ruta wondered if it cost too much. The assistant found the humidifier and said it cost thirty-one dollars, with delivery on Friday. "Yes, order it," Ruta typed. The assistant placed the order and said a message would come when the box left the shop. Ruta also asked what to do if the size was wrong, and the assistant said returns were free for thirty days.

Kofi was driving home when the phone screen began to glow with a new message. Kofi could not look, so Kofi said, "Read my last text." The assistant read it out: "We need rice, the cupboard is empty. Dinner is at seven." Kofi said, "Reply that the current traffic is bad and I will be there in eleven minutes." The assistant sent the reply. Then it asked if Kofi wanted to buy rice on the way. "Yes, find a shop near my route," Kofi said. The assistant named a small shop two streets ahead and gave directions by voice.

Nikola filmed a skate trick with an old digital camera and put the clip on the phone. The video looked too wide on the small screen. Nikola texted the assistant: "make this clip narrower but I don't want it cut shorter". The assistant changed the width to fit the screen and kept every second. Nikola could not decide who should see it first, so Nikola typed, "share it with Dara only, not the whole group". The assistant sent it to Dara and said it would tell Nikola when Dara watched it.

Nadia was a busy parent, and the kids were so excited about a trip in the morning that they would not sleep. At a quarter past eight, Nadia typed on the phone: "wake me at six and play soft muisc for the kids now". The assistant set the alarm for six. Then it started a playlist of slow music at a low volume in the bedroom. It also said it would turn the music off after thirty minutes. Nadia tiptoed out and the house slowly got quiet.

Someone wants a one-minute timer for a guessing game, where players paint or draw things like a toothbrush or an expensive car.
start a timer for a minute
sixty seconds on the clock please
time us for one minute
countdown, a minute, go
set a sixty second timer for our turn
can you time each round? one minute each
we need a minute per turn, tell us when it's up
could you please keep time for the game and ring when sixty seconds are over

name: photo_finder
does: Finds pictures in your albums by who is in them, where or when, and tracks which ones you have already shared.
inputs: a name, place, date or event, such as mother's birthday or a windy day at the beach
people say:
- show me the pictures from mum's birthday
- find that photo of the dog at the beach
- pull up last summer's trip
- where are the pictures I took on Saturday
- which photos haven't I sent to anyone yet
- I need the one with grandpa and the cake

Arjun was not good with technology, but wanted to plan the week's lunches. Arjun had swept crumbs from the floor near the vent and found the bread was stale. So Arjun said to the speaker, "I need less bread this week and double the soup. What can I eat for lunch?" The speaker made a plan: soup with rice on Monday and Wednesday, a salad on Tuesday, and eggs on toast on Thursday and Friday. It said it used half as much bread as last week. Arjun nodded and asked the speaker to put the plan on the fridge screen.

A robot mower cuts grass by itself. It is for people who don't want to push a mower around the lawn. It drives in lines, stays inside the edge, and goes home to charge. It is so quiet that it makes only a whisper. People change its hours by saying "mow in the morning" or "keep it off today". They say "clean up the edges" when the grass grows over the path. A sprinkler waters the lawn, and people say "water for ten minutes" or "skip the water, it rained". Some gardeners plant garlic along the garden beds, and ask the mower to stay out of that area.

Edward moved to the city only a week ago and still got lost. One evening Edward asked the tv, "Show me the top videos about the underground trains, from this year." Before the list loaded, Edward said, "Sorry, I mean the buses, not the trains." The tv changed the search and showed five videos about city buses. The first one, a clear map of the main routes, was at the top. Edward pressed play and wrote down the number of the bus that went near the new flat.

A podcast is a show you listen to in episodes. An audiobook is a book that is read aloud in chapters. Both remember where you left off, so you can wash dishes at the sink and keep listening. If a listener sneezes and misses a line, they say "go back thirty seconds". People change the speed by saying "play it faster" or "slow down a little". Some shows are free and others are paid. When people come back the next day, they ask "where did I leave off?" and the story starts at the right place.

Ananya was late. With an umbrella in one hand and keys in the other, Ananya said to the phone, "Play this week's top ranked pop songs, and don't play any slow ones." The phone started a fast playlist. Behind Ananya, the automatic light clicked off as the door closed. In the rain, the music kept going, and the phone skipped one slow song on its own. Ananya asked for the volume to go up a little, and the phone raised it a bit, just enough to hear over the rain.

Booking a hotel room means choosing a city, the nights you stay and how many guests will sleep there. It is for having a safe place to sleep and shower while you travel. People change the plan by saying "make it three nights", "for two guests", "the cheapest room" or "at least a quiet room". Check-in is the time when you may enter your room. Some hotels serve breakfast with fruit and vegetable dishes. Before leaving home, many people ask the assistant to remind them to pack their charger and to check the least busy time to arrive.

Stavros could not hear the speaker from the front room. It sat on a shelf by the front door, next to a muddy boot, and a paper tag on it said "ask me for help". Stavros was not good with technology, so Stavros typed on the phone: "turn the speker up in the hallway". The speaker became louder and said, "Is this volume okay?" Stavros typed, "a bit more", and the speaker raised it once more. Stavros smiled, sat down in the front room, and listened to the radio.

name: evening_check_in
does: Calls an older person every evening to ask if they are well, tells their family if nobody answers, and warns about rain before an evening walk; it can also say how many pills are left.
inputs: who to call, the evening time, and who to tell if there is no answer
people say:
- check on Grandma every evening
- call my dad at seven and tell me if he doesn't pick up
- make sure mum is okay tonight
- ring my aunt each night and let me know she's fine
- I want someone to look in on Grandpa after dinner

Before swimming at the beach, people check the tide, the water temperature and the sun. Sun cream protects your skin, and you put it on again every two hours. A noisy beach can make it hard to hear a lifeguard, so flags show if swimming is safe. Tides go in and out twice a day. People ask "when is high tide?", "is the water warm?" or "how strong is the sun?". Water that runs down from melting snow, through a channel to the sea, can make the sea near its mouth much colder, so people check the temperature first.

Freya was filling a bucket with weeds when a thought came. Freya wanted to call a cousin who lived far away and said to the phone, "What time is it in Sydney right now?" The phone said it was seven in the evening. "Oh wait, I mean Auckland, not Sydney," Freya said. The phone corrected itself: it was nine in the evening in Auckland. That was too late for a call, so Freya asked for a temporary reminder for tomorrow morning, just for this call. Then Freya went back to the garden to practice planting seedlings.

A clock shows the time where you are. Time zones mean that other places have different times. People use this for calling friends or planning trips. If your cousin lives far away, you might say "what time is it in Lima?" or "is it morning or night for Dad?". People can ask for a list of cities, like "show me three clocks". When you travel, you can say "set my clock to local time". Someone might say sorry for a late call because they forgot the difference. Even a bike ride across some borders can change the clock by an hour.

Person: Water leak.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Where is the leak?
Person: Bathroom, under the sink.
Assistant: Is the water still running?
Person: Yes. A spider ran away when I opened the cupboard, and then I saw the water.
Assistant: Okay. I can't turn off your water from here, because I'm not connected to your pipes. Look for the main valve. It is often close to the water meter.
Person: Where is the meter? I'm new to the city.
Assistant: Often in the basement or by the front door. Do you want me to find a plumber nearby?
Person: Yes please.

Jing, a retired teacher, hated it when the printer ran out of ink at a sudden moment. Today it happened again, while printing a grocery list for the church sale. Jing said to the tablet, "Order black ink and tell me how many pages are still waiting to print." The tablet ordered a new black ink cartridge from the usual shop. Then it said four pages were still in the line. Jing sighed, found an old cartridge in the drawer, and asked the tablet to start the printing again.

name: stop_near_me
does: Points you to the closest bus or train stop to where you are or to an address.
inputs: your place or a street address; on a cloudy or rainy day it can pick a stop with a shelter
people say:
- where's the nearest bus stop?
- how do I get to the station from here
- which stop is closest to Maple Street
- I'm lost, which way is the train
- find me a stop with a roof, it's pouring
- I'm walking to the market, where do I catch a bus

Person: It looks gray outside, and I only brought a thin shirt.
Assistant: Welcome! Do you want the weather for today? Which part of the city are you in?
Person: Near the old market. Back home the summers boil, so this feels cold.
Assistant: Today it is twelve degrees, with showers in the afternoon. A jacket would be a good idea.
Person: Thanks. Can you show me a video of how people dress there?
Assistant: I can't play videos from here, sorry. I can tell you that most people wear a coat and carry an umbrella. After the rain the air will be clean and cool.

Someone cut a thick apple pie crust to score it, then burned a finger on the hot dish, and wants to know what to do first.
burn on my finger, what now
how do I treat a small burn
cold water? how long do I keep it under
what should I do right now, I burnt my hand on the oven
my finger is red and stings, help
wat do i do for a burn quick
could you tell me the first steps for a small burn, please
do I need a bandage or just leave it open

Pilar ran into the dark living room, late for a call. "Switch on the lamp on the table," Pilar said. The lamp glowed. "Wait, I mean the ceiling light, not the lamp." The assistant turned the lamp off and the ceiling light on. The light was cold and bluish, so Pilar said, "Make it warmer." The ceiling light changed to a soft yellow. Pilar opened the laptop, sat down, and joined the call with a few seconds to spare.

After a morning jog, Leila stood by the pool. The cover was pulled tight, and the lock on the gate was cold in Leila's hand. "Start the pump and tell me how warm the water is," Leila said to the speaker. The pump started with a hum. The speaker said the water was twenty-four degrees, warm enough for a swim. Leila took the cover off, folded it, and put it by the fence.
